item.title: How Bears defense solved Jaxon Smith-Njigba problem in win over Seahawks
item.description: How Bears defense solved Jaxon Smith-Njigba problem in win over Seahawks originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While wins and losses are the primary metric used by evaluators to determine whether a week was successful or not in the NFL, individual matchups most certainly matters. The final game of the Week 9 slate presented an enchanting one for NFL hardcores — Seahawks star Jaxon Smith-Njigba against anyone who the Bears lined up against him. Smith-Njigba is football's best receiver. His place at the top of that ladder hasn't been under question since the start of last year. And yet, there's a case — albeit a quiet one — that Chicago made him looking decidedly more ordinary than usual in its 34-17 win. Here's how the Bears bottled up Smith-Njigba to propel Ben Johnson's side to a famous win over Seattle. MORE: How delay of game penalty somehow helped Bears secure 'MNF' win How Bears defense found answer for Jaxon Smith-Njigba problem Chicago's defense proved unable to blight Smith-Njigba's influence in the first half. He was the lone light in Seattle's offense through two quarters, accounting for 92 of Sam Darnold's first 94 passing yards. Smith-Njigba found the end zone with one of his patented double moves, undressing Tyrique Stevenson as he did so. He had left Jaylon Johnson looking similarly foolish earlier in the affair. extremely sick https://t.co/YJQnbrKd5u — NFL (@NFL) November 3, 2026 On pace for nearly 200 yards at half, Smith-Njigba seemed the likeliest candidate to cause any sort of threat to Chicago's secondary. But as the second half wore on, Smith-Njigba found it increasingly harder to affect the game. After making four catches for 92 yards in the first half, the Ohio State product was held without a catch (or target) until Seattle's final offensive drive. Smith-Njigba might have been slightly unlucky to receive that distinction. He appeared to bring the Seahawks on the cusp of the goal line at the end of the third quarter, only to be whistled for what appeared to be a dubious offensive pass interference call. MORE: Jeffery Simmons announces his presence with dominant start to Bears career Jaxon Smith-Njigba called for OPI and Seahawks fans are FURIOUS https://t.co/lLN8NrTx9P — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 3, 2026 Nevertheless, Seattle just wasn't able to get Smith-Njigba involved in the action the way it intended heading into the contest. Some of that was Darnold's doing; he struggled for much of the contest. Chicago's secondary stepped up in a major way. So, too, did its defensive line; Jeffrey Simmons looked like the best player on the field for large portions of Monday's action. The Mississippi State alum recorded one sack, two tackles for loss and six tackles in his Bears debut. Darnold felt the pressure early and often on Monday night. Smith-Njigba had the minerals to leave his markers frustrated. But Darnold's inability to find him on a steady basis

item.title: Zelda Ocarina of Time release time in your time zone
item.description: The Zelda Ocarina of Time remake release time is just around the corner, as Nintendo introduces a new generation to one of its classic games. Unlike the 3DS port from 2011, Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 includes a massive visual overhaul, along with several quality-of-life features that weren't present in the original Nintendo 64 release. Pre-orders are still open at some retailers if you're hoping to snag a special bonus, though US-based folks only get one bonus to choose from.

item.title: 20 Years Later, Uncle Iroh's Wisest 'Avatar: The Last Airbender Quote' Is Still Undefeated
item.description: Avatar: The Last Airbender has more than its fair share of heartfelt moments and poignant lines. Whether it’s Aang reassuring a downtrodden Toph in the vast loneliness of the desert, or Ursa’s parting words to her son Zuko before disappearing in the middle of the night, the series can be surprisingly deep for what some might (incorrectly) consider a mere children’s show. No character embodies that richness and depth more than Uncle Iroh, who begins as Zuko's wise mentor and becomes so much more. Time and again, Iroh sits at the center of The Last Airbender 's most moving moments, offering quiet wisdom just when it's needed most.

item.title: Kane Exits With Injury in Blackhawks 5-2 Loss To Avalanche
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (4-10-1) blew a multi-goal lead for the second straight game, giving up five unanswered goals in a 5-2 loss to the Colorado Avalanche (9-5-1) at the United Center. The Blackhawks have now lost six of their last seven games Wyatt Kaiser and Roman Kantserov scored to give the Blackhawks a 2-0 lead just 7:05 into the game, but the Avalanche defense and goaltender Mackenzie Blackwood shut them down over the final 52:55. That’s now six of the last seven games in which they’ve failed to score three goals. Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz each scored twice for Colorado, who’ve now won 14 of 18 meetings with the Blackhawks since the start of 2022. Blackwood stopped 21 of 23 shots to earn the win in net, while Devon Toews scored the empty netter. To make matters worse, the Blackhawks lost star forward Patrick Kane due to injury in the second period, with head coach Jeff Blashill announcing the future Hall of Famer will miss the next couple of games with an upper-body issue. The Blackhawks have a three-game road trip ahead on the schedule, where they’ll face the Florida Panthers, Tampa Bay Lightning, and Carolina Hurricanes. Even with Kane in the lineup, winning any of those games would be challenging. Now, the Blackhawks are put in an even greater bind without one of their premier forwards. Here are highlights from the Blackhawks 5-2 loss to the Avalanche, dropping their 2026-27 regular-season record to 4-10-1 in 15 games. First Period Kaiser’s wrist shot from the point was deflected, but the puck still trickled across the goal line just 57 seconds in, giving the Blackhawks an early 1-0 lead. Kaiser has now recorded a point in three of his last four games and has two goals this season. Chicago has scored first in five of the last six outings. Connor Bedard➡️Ryan Donato➡️Wyatt Kaiser🚨 Kaiser’s point shot finds its way into the net to put the #Blackhawks ahead 1-0 early! It’s Kaiser’s 2nd goal of the season. Bedard extends his point streak to 6 games with the secondary assist. pic.twitter.com/yhCrGJi5pE — Talkin’ Hawkey (@TalkinHawkey) November 3, 2026 Kantserov doubled the Blackhawks’ lead at 7:05, burying a pass from Bedard on a 2-on-1 rush for his team-leading sixth goal of the season. 2-0, Chicago. Kantserov extended his point streak to five games with the goal. Bedard extended his point streak to six games with the assist. Connor Bedard➡️Roman Kantserov🚨 Kantserov nets his team-leading 6th goal of the season on a 2-on-1 with Bedard! Kantserov extends his point streak to 5 games. Bedard extends his to 6 games. 2-0 #Blackhawks . pic.twitter.com/pK669deolm — Talkin’ Hawkey (@TalkinHawkey) November 3, 2026 Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog put the puck on net from a sharp angle, and Kadri dove into the crease and knocked it home at 15:23, cutting the Blackhawks’ lead in half. 2-1. item.title: Duke Shells Army In Cameron By 34
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 02: Bryson Howard #12 of the Duke Blue Devils dunks the ball during the second half of the game against the Army Black Knights at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 02, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Alex Halloway/Getty Images) | Getty Images I t wasn’t an inspirational season opener or anything, but Duke beat Army, 84-50. And while it wasn’t a beautiful game – in fact, there were some obvious flaws – there was still a lot to discuss. So let’s just jump in. First, Duke held Army to 18-52 from the floor (35 percent) and 8-30 from the line (27 percent). Yes, it was Army, yes Duke had a major talent and size advantage, but even so, that’s indicative of pretty good defense. Army is a disciplined team, as you might expect, but even so, Duke’s defense was solid. Army had a total of 24 turnovers and at least six shot clock violations. There was some serious pressure on the Black Knights. Of the Army starters, Kevin McCarthy hit 6-11. The rest of the starters hit 7-40. Duke also had 16 steals and 6 blocks. Offense was another matter. Duke did start off with a 12-0 lead and shut Army out for nearly six minutes. The Blue Devils outscored Army in the paint, 50-20, and won the boards, 37-25. Dame Sarr, with 16 points, and Patrick Ngongba, with 10 points and 7 rebounds, led the way for the Blue Devils. Duke hadn’t had a game with zero made threes since December 30, 1989, against Hawaii. Jon Scheyer was two years old at the time. For a long time, it looked like that streak might come to an end. Duke missed all of its attempts in the first half before Cayden Boozer hit one. Duke wound up shooting 4-22 from behind the line. JoJo Boumtje Boumtje hit 1-4, and John Blackwell hit 1-5. He was back on the court after the game, ironing out the bugs. He’s also strong enough to drive successfully, and now that he can hit from the line (last year he shot 53.2 percent from the line. He’s a vastly more versatile offensive weapon now. So offense wasn’t that great. But here’s something interesting: Against Army, Dame Sarr hit 6-6. In the three preseason games, he hit 9-10 against Belmont, 2-3 against Tennessee, and 8-11 against Kansas. Obviously, the exhibition games don’t count, but still, over those four games, he’s shooting 83.3 percent from the line. We also saw Drew Scharnowski make his season debut. He got eight minutes off the bench, had 4 points, 2 rebounds, an assist and a steal. He looked pretty solid. Deron Rippey had two spectacular plays: on one break, he bobbled the ball, caught up to it, and nailed a behind-the-back pass to Sarr for a layup, and got a dunk on a rebound. Caleb Foster came in and played hard, especially on defense. At one point, he was guarding Army’s 6-9 Tate Laczkowski, and while he was at a disadvantage, the way he kept waving his arms made us think about what he must have been like as a little kid. You could imagine him doing the same thing with a big brother or an older kid down the street. So it

item.title: Volleyball Splits Road Action over Spooky Weekend
item.description: After a rough homecoming performance at McCamish Pavilion, in which the Jackets were swept by both #2 Pitt and #7 SMU, the Jackets hit the road over Halloween weekend to face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and the #3 Louisville Cardinals. The Jackets split the weekend, completing a dramatic reverse sweep of Notre Dame before falling to the Cardinals in straight sets. This puts the Jackets at 14-8 on the year and 6-5 in the ACC, keeping pace in the conference and showing notable improvement over last season. VS Notre Dame Unlike their football (and lacrosse and fencing teams, which are apparently even more dominant than football), the Notre Dame volleyball team is, well, terrible. The Irish entered the matchup against the Jackets at a miserable 4-15, including 1-9 in ACC play. That was good for second-to-last in the ACC, ahead of a somehow even worse Syracuse team, which had provided the Irish with their sole Power Four win of the year. The point is, this should have been a walk in the park for the Jackets, and yet, two sets in, Tech was on the verge of being swept. Set 1: (0-0): The Irish controlled the entire first set, relinquishing the lead to Tech just once before quickly snatching it back. While Tech stayed within striking distance, never trailing by more than five and getting as close as 21-23 late, it was ultimately for naught as Notre Dame cruised to a four-point victory. The Irish ran an incredibly clean operation, hitting .433 on the set and tallying just three total errors to the Jackets’ 11. Alida Bennour was largely responsible for keeping Tech alive, contributing nine kills and an ace. Set 2: (1-0, Notre Dame) The second set was more of a back-and-forth affair that featured five lead changes and 14 ties. Both squads hit around .100 in an ugly showing that saw the Jackets brutally play down to their competition. While Tech once again had a shot to take the lead late with the score knotted up at 23, they squandered it again as the Irish went on another 2-0 run, capitalized by a 42-second rally that ended with yet another Tech attack error, of which they had 10 in the set. Set 3: (2-0, Notre Dame) It seemed like we’d be in for another close affair early in the third set, with Tech leading by just one through the first 15 points. The Jackets tried to create separation, but the Irish held them close, allowing Tech to take just a 15-12 lead midway through the set. Tech finally found the separation it was looking for after an 8-1 run punctuated by three consecutive kills by Mia Hood. They won the set 25-15, this time capitalizing on another sub .100 hitting percentage by the Irish. Set 4: (2-1, Notre Dame) Notre Dame completely abandoned the disciplined form they had shown earlier, committing 12 attack errors and posting a negative .111 hitting percentage on the set. item.title: Rob Wright, BYU Offense Shine in Opening Night Win Over Ohio State
item.description: SALT LAKE CITY, UT - NOVEMBER 2: Robert Wright III #1 of the Brigham Young Cougars drives the ball the court against Justin Pippen #10 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the first half of their game at the Delta Center on November 2, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images After scoring just 16 points in the first 13 minutes, BYU’s offense woke up in a big way the rest of the game in a 94-83 win over Ohio State on the opening day of college basketball. BYU was down 37-34 at halftime and trailed by as much as 11, but BYU outscored the Buckeyes 60-46 in the second half. Rob Wright was sensational and looked like an All-American, leading BYU with 33 points, 5 assists, and 1 turnover on 9/15 shooting from the field (4/5 from three) and 11/12 from the line. Rob showed his whole bag, getting into the paint, finishing around the rim and with floaters, and hitting pullup and stepback threes. All five BYU starters scored in double figures. Tyler Betsey was 4/5 from three and scored 15 points, Collin Chandler scored 15 points as well, Bruce Branch put up 12 after a slow start, and Jaxon Kohler scored 11 points. BYU played four guys off the bench, who scored a combined 8 points. Nate Pickens made a three to end the first half and Brooks Bahr played nice defense on Ohio State’s best player, John Mobley. BYU shot 54% compared to 49% from Ohio State, shot 11/24 (46%) from three, and won the turnover battle 12-8. BYU’s defense didn’t play great, but they did enough and came up with a few good stretches to allow them to extend the league. BYU’s lack of rim protection will put a ceiling on the defense, and Ohio State exposed that at times around the rim. This game should hold up as a Quad 1 win for BYU and be a nice data point on the resume. Ohio State came into the game ranked 18 in KenPom and BYU 33. BYU jumped to 22 after the win. BYU next plays Omaha Friday night in Provo and has the runway to be 5-0 going into the Maui Invitational in 3 weeks.

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba receiving yards pace: How Seahawks WR can catch Calvin Johnson, Cooper Kupp
item.description: Jaxon Smith-Njigba receiving yards pace: How Seahawks WR can catch Calvin Johnson, Cooper Kupp originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Somehow, Jaxon Smith-Njigba may be even more dominant this season than he was in 2025. The Seahawks receiver has stamped himself as the NFL's best offensive weapon, coming off an outstanding 2025 season in which he was named Offensive Player of the Year while helping lead Seattle to a Super Bowl title. But through the first seven games of 2026, Smith-Njigba could be on pace for history. Last year, he finished No. 8 on the all-time leaderboard for single-season receiving yards with 1,793. This year, he's not only on pace to shatter that mark for a new career-high — he could contend for Calvin Johnson's record. Here's a look at where Smith-Njigba's pace stands against Johnson's historic 2012 season. MORE: Ranking 12 best potential deals for NFL playoff contenders in 2026 Jaxon Smith-Njigba stats 2026 Catches: 64 Receiving Yards: 985 Yards Per Catch: 15.4 Yards Per Game: 123.2 TDs: 9 If you thought Smith-Njigba was dominant in 2025, he's reached all-time levels in 2026. Through eight games, he is on pace to shatter his career-highs in catches, yards and touchdowns, all set last season. He's already just one touchdown shy of his entire 2025 total over 17 games. And he's been the full engine of Seattle's offense — the run game ranks around the middle of the NFL with 109.6 yards per game, yet Smith-Njigba is accountable for more yards than all other Seahawks receivers combined. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 959 yards receiving and 9 TD catches this season. Only other players since at least 1948 to do that in first 8 games of a season: Torry Holt 978 and 9 in 2003 Raymond Berry 966 and 9 in 1960 Elroy Hirsch 1,058 and 12 in 1951 — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) November 3, 2026 Whether it's been down the field, in short-range or in the red zone, Smith-Njigba has handled about as much as one receiver can in the NFL despite consistently drawing the full attention of defenses. And at his current pace of 123.2 yards per game, he'd make NFL history without even needing a 17th game. Here's more to know about Smith-Njigba's pace. How many yards does Jaxon Smith-Njigba need to pass Calvin Johnson? It's still fairly early in the record chance, but entering Week 8, Smith-Njigba is 979 yards away from tying, and 980 yards away from breaking, Johnson's 2012 record of 1,964 receiving yards. In 2012, Johnson averaged 122.8 yards per game over 16 games. That means Smith-Njigba is currently out-pacing him — and if he maintains that pace, he wouldn't even need a 17th game to break the record. Smith-Njigba would reach 1,970 yards by the Seahawks' 16th game. After a 17th game, he would be on pace to clear 2,090 yards, shattering the single-season record. item.title: Marist football miss late FG try, fall at San Diego
item.description: Marist missed a field goal try with 43 seconds left in regulation and bowed to San Diego, 41-40, at Torero Stadium on Saturday, October 31. Consecutive losses have dropped Marist to 4-5 and 3-2 in the Pioneer Football League. San Diego bumped to 4-5, 3-3. The Red Foxes trailed 35-26 headed into the fourth quarter and produced a pair of touchdowns, the last on a 51-yard run by Isaiah Simmons (his second of the game, the first on a stutter-step move from 35 yards) with 6:17 left for a 40-35 lead - he finished with 182 yards on 21 carries. Simmons took a handoff to the right side and cut inside a block and ran untouched. The Toreros used a no-huddle offense to move 65 yards on nine plays. USD quarterback Dom Nankil completed four of five throws and ran the final 4 yards for the go-ahead touchdown, faking a handoff, deking one tackler and diving in with 2:48 to play (a 2-point conversion failed). Logan Johnson returned the ensuing kickoff 28 yards to the Marist 33. Quarterback Sonny Mannino gained a trio of first downs, the first on his own 4-yard run on fourth down and following with completions of 10 and 28 yards to Zach Garmont, down to the San Diego 19. Simmons gained 8 yards up the middle but then suffered a 3-yard loss. Lincoln Cardillo was stopped shy of the first down, and Luke Stenson was called on for a 30-yard field goal try but missed. Mannino passed for 265 yards and ran for 34. Sophomore defensive back Jace Williamson set the school's Div. I single-game mark with 22 tackles. Marist took a 19-7 lead midway through the second quarter but the Toreros scored the next 21 points, and eventually took a 35-26 lead into the fourth. But the Red Foxes responded with a pair of touchdowns, San Diego improved to 17-2 all-time against Marist, including all 12 games at home. Marist closes with home games against Morehead State on Nov. 7 and Butler on Nov. 14 and a road contest at Davidson on Nov. 21. kmcmillan@th-record.com X / Twitter: @KenMcMillanTHR This article originally appeared on Times Herald-Record: Marist football miss late FG try, fall at San Diego

item.title: Why NASCAR's indecision led to Dodge's decision to return to Cup
item.description: Motorsport photo Dodge is coming back to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027 with Kaulig Racing but there are caveats aplenty. The body has been approved, with an unveil scheduled for the Snowball Derby Super Late race in December, but the engine inside of the car is not expected to be a proprietary Stellantis or MOPAR built platform. Current reporting suggests AJ Allmendinger and Ty Dillon will drive cars powered by Earnhardt Childress Racing Engines next season. In some ways, NASCAR was fortunate in that Stellantis was only interested in racing right now using an internal combustion gasoline platform that aligned with the 'HEMI is Back' initiative from the manufacturer. It wasn't that long ago that NASCAR was seriously all-in towards electric and hybrid before the culture domestically shifted. Stellantis, Dodge and RAM reflects that shift and NASCAR hadn't yet jumped into the EV space. NASCAR Event Management president John Probst said that wasn’t a selling point to Stellantis but all parties benefited from the timing. "I'd like to pretend we had some big scheme that made that all look good, but it's just like a lot of things in life," Probst said. "Sometimes it's just timing works out and you're aligned, and this is the example of that." Probst also said that at a minimum, NASCAR will retain its current engine regulations through 2028 but also could extend it through 2030 or 2032. In other words, there were few reasons for Dodge to build their own engine just to have to do it again in two to five years. So again, the timing just made sense for Dodge. Probst conceded that they nearly prematurely ended up with an EV platform at the moment the country turned on them. Thus, NASCAR is being thoughtful about what comes next. "I would say that right now we have started discussions with the OEMs about what does our future look like around the engine," Probst said. "I would say that we're targeting anywhere from 2030-to-2032, and that may sound a little wishy-washy, I guess, on the specific date, but as we talk through the OEMs, we've already had our first meeting. We're onto our second meeting here coming up real soon to try and figure out where we want to go as a sport. "And I think that some of that is looking at the broader landscape around what's going on in the motor sport world and us, what do we want to do, frankly, around our engine? If you look around the landscape, there's certainly been a lot of vacillation around how much of the powertrain should be electrified. So, we just want to make sure that we don't rush into something. "If we would've rushed in a few years ago, we'd add a big hybrid component to the car. And I think that there's just a lot that goes into it. So I guess it's a lot of words for probably what could have been a quick answer. 2030 to 2032 is the window we're looking at." With those parameters in mind, Dodge just needed to get a body approved, and Stellantis pushed NASCAR hard to not get shoe boxed into the 2028 timeline the Sa

item.title: Swift, Simmons star as Bears maul Seahawks
item.description: D'Andre Swift rushes for one of his three touchdowns in Chicago's road victory over Seattle (Steph Chambers) D'Andre Swift rushed for three touchdowns as the Chicago Bears overpowered the Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in a statement road victory over the reigning Super Bowl champions on Monday. Chicago running back Swift scored all three of his touchdowns in the second half at Seattle's Lumen Field, two of them coming in the fourth quarter as the Seahawks threatened a comeback. A rampant Chicago defense led by newly signed defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons also helped shut down Seattle's offense. Simmons, traded to the Bears last week from the Tennessee Titans, enjoyed a dream debut with six tackles and a sack. "I'm so excited to be a Chicago Bear man," Simmons told ESPN. "This is just the beginning. We've got some stuff to clean up but it's a good football team and I’m happy to be a part of it." Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams finished with 247 passing yards with 24-of-34 completions and one touchdown. Swift had 69 yards from 27 carries for his three touchdowns. Seattle fell to 4-4 to lose further ground in the NFC West behind San Francisco (6-1). The Bears set the tone for an impressive win in the first quarter when Williams led a 17-play 80-yard drive that ended with a touchdown pass to Luther Burden. Seattle kicker Jason Myers got Seattle's first points with a 27-yard field goal but Chicago responded with back-to-back three-pointers from Cairo Santos to leave the Bears 13-3 up. Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold found Jaxon Smith-Njigba with a 43-yard pass to leave Seattle only four points adrift at the break. But Swift capped another long Chicago drive to score his first touchdown in the third quarter and give the Bears a comfortable 20-9 lead. Seattle responded with a Cooper Kupp touchdown early in the fourth quarter but Chicago's defense took over and Swift bagged two touchdowns to seal victory. rcw/pst

item.title: NFL world reacts to Bears' dominant 34-17 win vs. Seahawks
item.description: The Chicago Bears made another statement on the prime-time stage with a dominant 34-17 win over the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks to improve to 6-2 on the season, where the team's biggest playmakers, quarterback Caleb Williams and new defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, shined. Simmons' debut with Chicago couldn't have gone better, as he tied for a team-high six tackles, including two tackles for loss, one sack, one QB hit and one pass breakup in what was a sensational defensive showing. He opened up things for players around him, most notably former college teammate Montez Sweat, who had one sack and three QB hits. Simmons is already proving to be worth those two first-round picks (and perhaps more). Meanwhile, Williams cemented himself in the MVP conversation after putting on a show against a dominant Seahawks defense. He completed 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards with one touchdown, no turnovers and a 101 passer rating. Williams became the first quarterback to throw for more than 200 yards against this Seattle defense this season. In the last two weeks, Chicago has beaten the defending AFC Champions (New England Patriots) and reigning Super Bowl champions (Seahawks). This was the kind of statement win that shows that this Bears team is a legitimate Super Bowl contender, and fans from around the NFL agree. item.title: How Bears benefitted from own delay of game penalty to secure win over Seahawks
item.description: How Bears benefitted from own delay of game penalty to secure win over Seahawks originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . They say "when it rains, it pours," but it's the opposite for the Bears right now. On Monday night, even what didn't go well turned out well for the Bears in a 34-17 win over the defending-champion Seahawks . A delay of game penalty in the fourth quarter looked like it would keep the momentum with Seattle in a one-possession game, but it instead turned into the extra chance Chicago needed to jumpstart a drive and bury the Seahawks. Here's what you need to know about how the Bears benefitted from their own penalty. MORE: Jeffery Simmons shines in Bears debut Bears delay of game penalty The Seahawks, trailing by three, appeared to have a stop and a chance to get the ball back before they realized officials had blown a third down play dead with a delay of game penalty. Because the penalty occurred before the snap, the tackle for loss that would've easily forced fourth down was erased, and the Bears had a chance to extend their drive on third-and-9. The 3rd & 4 delay of game on what would have been a tackle for loss into the 3rd & 9 Kalif Raymond explosive could be the biggest sliding doors moment for the NFC playoff picture this season. Am in shock — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) November 3, 2026 Kalif Raymond exploded for 39 yards, not only extending the drive but setting up a Bears touchdown that would stretch the lead to two possessions just seconds later. When you call a screen you hope it’s blocked up as well as this was. Big-time play by Chicago. https://t.co/n19LGEi43s — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) November 3, 2026 Because the penalty occurred before the snap, the Seahawks weren't able to decline it. With the crowd tempered, the Seahawks never recovered from the sequence. Seattle wouldn't score again, ultimately giving up another touchdown as the Bears jumped out to a 17-point advantage. item.title: Florida State dominates FAMU in season opener, 112-69
item.description: We are so back. Florida State (0-0, 0-0 ACC) played Florida A&M (0-0, 0-0 SWAC) in Tampa as part of the Orion180 Tipoff Classic on Monday night. The Seminoles, looking to build on a top-20 recruiting class and start the season off right, did just that, winning 112-69 to move to 1-0. First Half It was a disappointing first half if you consider three-pointers. The Seminoles made just three of 12 triples. However, they excelled in virtually every other category. FSU kept their foot on the gas and never looked back, as there were zero lead changes whatsoever. Not much to say in terms of this game being competitive; the closest the game got was 13-8. It was all FSU from there on out. Marcis Ponder got seven boards in the first half alone, while also tacking on five two-pointers and five made free throws. He also got the lone block for Florida State. Second Half After the poor shooting performance in the first, the second was admittedly better, as they finished at 8/24 for 33% of their made threes. The defense looked like last year’s team but only way better and with more size behind it. The bench also showed some promise; Brandon Bass Jr. and Martay Barnes led with 13 and 10 points, respectively. Alex Steen was six and seven in points and rebounds (get it?), while Cooper Schwieger scored six points and got two rebounds. The Seminoles finished with an offensive rating of 142.4 and a defensive efficiency rating of 87.7. Yes, it’s a SWAC non-conference game. Finishing with seven total turnovers is absurd, even against a weaker team. If they keep up this pace, even somewhat against Troy or even Florida, this could be a very scary team. Players of the Game Sebastian Rancik was in a league of his own with 25 points in just 27 minutes, a new career high for him. I’d also like to shout out Marcis Ponder for dropping 15 points and 11 rebounds. What’s Next? Florida State returns home to Tallahassee for their home opener against the Troy Trojans, a tournament team in 2025, on November 6th. Fans can catch that game on the ACC Network Extra. Then it’s a huge home game against the No. 1 team in the land, *thunder sound effect* , the Florida Gators, followed by a gimme game versus Texas A&M Corpus Christi.

item.title: Diamondbacks rumors: Insider gets 100% real on challenge of potential Ketel Marte trade
item.description: Credit: Arianna Grainey-Imagn Images Diamondbacks rumors: Insider gets 100% real on challenge of potential Ketel Marte trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Diamondbacks just narrowly missed out on the 2026 MLB postseason, which means that they don’t have to overhaul the roster to try and finally get over that hump. The what-if game, however, is dangerous for the Diamondbacks to play. After all, they might have gotten the two more wins they needed to quality for this year’s postseason if it weren’t for the sudden and unexplained absence from Ketel Marte , the slugging infielder. Now, it looks as though the Diamondbacks are looking to put up a more conscious effort to trade Marte away after a drama-filled 2026 campaign. However, MLB insider Jim Bowden warned Arizona that it might not be very easy to trade the 33-year-old away, especially when he has a no-trade clause. “If he decides that he doesn’t want to get traded, then he won’t be,” Bowden said. “You gotta find a team that not only that he’s willing to go to, but you gotta find a front office, a GM, a manager, and a group of players that are willing to accept all the things that come with Ketel Marte, which includes times where players, some teammates, have been disappointed that he didn’t take the field.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Trading Ketel Marte is A LOT easier said than done. @JimBowdenGM breaks down the no-trade clause, the contract, and everything a team would have to weigh before making a deal. pic.twitter.com/IJWNBJxihC — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) November 2, 2026 Marte missed the Diamondbacks’ August 17 clash against the Boston Red Sox despite being penciled into the starting lineup, and this absence of his stunned the organization. He would miss 13 consecutive games for the Dbacks in the middle of a postseason push, and during this stretch, Arizona went 7-6. Marte has at least four more seasons left on his contract for a total of $77.5 million in guaranteed money, and he has a player option for $11.5 million in 2031, when he’s entering his age-37 campaign. Coupled with his decline in production (his OPS of .748 in 2026 is down from his .893 OPS in 2025), the Diamondbacks may have to eat a portion of his contract to find him a new home, provided, of course, that he waives his no-trade clause. Related: Diamondbacks lands news bullpen coach from Padres Related: Diamondbacks star Corbin Burnes staying with Arizona after injury-plagued season

item.title: 'He grabbed me': Fan whose drink LeBron James took a sip of details what actually happened
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images LeBron James taking a sip of a fan’s drink has become the biggest talking point from the game between the Philadelphia 76ers and the Chicago Bulls. The Sixers continued their incredible run by beating the Bulls 126-107. They are now 7-1 this season and are the absolute favourites to reach the final. James had a very good game, but as soon as he grabbed a fan’s drink, he probably knew that was going to make the headlines. The said fan has now had his say. Fan details what happened before LeBron James took a sip of his drink Fans buy courtside seats to be as close to their heroes and the game as possible, but Troy Clemons got a lot more than he ever imagined. A longtime Sixers season-ticket holder, Clemons was walking back to his seat with a drink in his hand, and James crashed into him. The wine spilt everywhere, but to his surprise, the 76ers superstar grabbed it and took a sip of it before heading back on the court to continue playing. All eyes were on Clemons at that point, and he spoke to Kris Rhim about what really happened. He said: “I was walking to my seat with whatever beverage this is, we won’t say what it is, and LeBron crashed into me. He grabbed me, and he said: “My bad!” My drink spilt everywhere. “He took my drink from me, and he basically took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back to the field. I’m just glad for him to be here. I’m not worried about the wine getting on me.” A glass that James took a sip from in the middle of an NBA game would’ve been good memorabilia for many fans to hold on to or even sell. However, Clemons didn’t even consider that and threw the glass in the bin before grabbing another one. “At the end of the day, he’s another man like me,” he said. “I mean, he’s LeBron, but I threw the cup in the trash. It’s nothing up with him. I just got a fresh drink.” Read more: ‘I’m no Steph Curry’ – LeBron James nearly lost to MrBeast in a $100,000 three-point challenge Isiah Thomas snubs Michael Jordan, picks LeBron James and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar in GOAT debate LeBron James fans uncover Angel Reese’s 2021 shot at 76ers star after Dream’s loss in WNBA Finals

item.title: Dortmund bring back painful memories for evergreen Pellegrini
item.description: Real Betis coach Manuel Pellegrini heads back to the scene of one of the most painful nights of his career (JORGE GUERRERO) Veteran Real Betis coach Manuel Pellegrini has regularly produced impressive results at the highest level but his failure to win the Champions League means some hesitate to place him among the managerial elite. The 73-year-old's team boast three wins from three in the league phase ahead of Wednesday's visit to face Borussia Dortmund, the scene of one of the most agonising defeats in his long career. In 2013 Pellegrini's Malaga conceded twice in injury time against Jurgen Klopp's Dortmund, to miss out on a Champions League semi-final berth. It was an especially cruel defeat for Pellegrini, who had attended his father's funeral in Chile before landing in Germany on the morning of the match. "They did not want us in the semi-finals," complained Pellegrini about the officiating afterwards, with Felipe Santana's winner seemingly scored from an offside position. That summer Pellegrini moved to Manchester City, winning the Premier League and two League Cups before departing in 2016, without a Champions League trophy. The evergreen Chilean joined Betis in 2020 and is now enjoying the longest spell in charge of a club in his career. Pellegrini has stayed faithful to the idea that his teams must entertain and Betis fit the bill, boasting a host of exciting attackers like Isco and Ez Abde. Pellegrini, who graduated in civil engineering in 1979 while playing at Universidad de Chile, took Betis to their first final in 17 years, winning the Copa del Rey in 2022. Last season he steered the Andalusians back to Champions League qualification after two decades away from the elite. "We started the first match of the season... and at the end of the team talk we wrote in green letters -- 'today we begin our journey to the Champions League'," explained Pellegrini in May. - 'My own' way - Pellegrini returning Betis to the big-time is no surprise, given his track record. The coach turned Villarreal into a Champions League semi-finalist in 2006, with his team knocked out by Arsenal. Juan Roman Riquelme missed a last-gasp penalty in the second leg which could have taken the game to extra-time on Spain's east coast. Pellegrini led Villarreal to a second-place finish in La Liga in 2008, finishing above giants Barcelona and Atletico Madrid. His success earned him the Real Madrid job in 2009, where he achieved a then-club record 96 points, but was sacked at the end of the season to make way for Jose Mourinho. Madrid chief Florentino Perez was desperate for the club's 10th Champions League trophy and thought the Portuguese would deliver it. Later at City, he was replaced by Pep Guardiola. After Madrid, Pellegrini helped Malaga reach the Champions League for the first and only time in their history, with their journey ending in Dortmund. item.title: Demichelis brings 'competitive aura' to Leipzig before City reunion
item.description: RB Leipzig coach Martin Demichelis will face his former side Manchester City on Wednesday (Javier SORIANO) Coach Martin Demichelis will be looking to strike a blow against his former employers when his RB Leipzig side host Manchester City in the Champions League on Wednesday. Former Argentina centre-back Demichelis spent three seasons at Manchester City, winning the 2013-14 Premier League title and two League Cups. Demichelis, who also won four league titles as a player at Bayern Munich, is now hoping to bring success to Saxony in a budding coaching career. Leipzig have beaten City just once in six attempts, but may feel Enzo Maresca's men are vulnerable. In their past three games, City have lost twice and won the other match on penalties, as the spectre of sanctions for breaching financial rules looms. Demichelis, 45, was controversially handpicked by then-Red Bull boss Jurgen Klopp to take over in the summer. To bring in Demichelis, Leipzig sacked popular coach Ole Werner, who had taken a young team back into the Champions League, while overseeing the development of Yan Diomande. Real Madrid paid a reported 125 million euros ($140 million) for Diomande, just a year after Leipzig signed him for 20 million euros. Demichelis was relegated from La Liga during a short stint with Mallorca last season but Klopp and Leipzig had seen enough to convince them of his ability, after he oversaw a significant up-turn in the club's form. After a rocky start with Leipzig including a 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League and a 6-1 thrashing by Bayern Munich, Leipzig have won three games in a row. The Red Bulls sit just three points off top spot in the Bundesliga, but are in desperate need of points in Europe. The 2020 semi-finalists are 29th in the 36-team table after winning just one of three Champions League games this campaign. - 'Competitive aura' - Demichelis benefited from the tutelage of several big-name coaches, including Louis van Gaal, Manuel Pellegrini, Diego Simeone and his idol Diego Maradona. Leipzig centre-back Maxime Esteve said Demichelis has brought a "competitive aura" to the club. "Even in small games in training, you can see that the coach does not want to lose," Esteve told AFP and other media on Monday. "When he misses something, you can see he's a little bit angry. You can see he stopped playing football not that long ago. "You can see the aura of his competitiveness." Esteve played under another former City player, Vincent Kompany, during his time at Burnley and said Demichelis reminds him of the Belgian, who is now coach of Bayern. "It's funny because they both spend a lot of time in the gym. They want to stay fit, because they have a big history in football. "They play in games in training and you can see they are quite competitive. They don't want to lose. "They are really energetic and spend a lot of time at the training ground. "They are perfectionists and want to sort out the small details as soon as they can." Esteve also has e

item.title: Boston Celtics falter vs. Houston Rockets, 109-93, in second loss of season
item.description: The Boston Celtics' winning ways were halted by the Houston Rockets on Monday evening at the Toyota Center. The C's shot just under 39 percent from the floor in Texas and the Rockets handed them a 109-93 loss, snapping Boston's five-game winning streak. Although the Celtics were playing on the second night of a back-to-back, they had a chance at upsetting the Western Conference-leading Rockets. However, no Celtic could even reach 20 points and Boston was heavily outscored in the paint (50-34) and in transition (18-2). Celtics star Jayson Tatum recorded a team-high 19 points while Rockets center Alperen Şengün notched 26 points, missing only 3 of his 15 field goal attempts in the process. The Celtics are now 5-2 and headed back home to face the struggling Milwaukee Bucks at TD Garden. Meanwhile, the Rockets sit atop the West at 7-1 and are off to their best start through eight games in over a decade. Before Boston looks to bounce back in Beantown, let's take a look at the most memorable moments from Monday night's battle captured in images below. item.title: Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN
item.description: •Demand deposits climb 71% •Analysts highlight cash dependence, financial inclusion challenges By Peter Egwuatu Currency held outside the banking system by Nigerians rose by 103.8 per cent to N4.923 trillion in September 2026 from N2.416 trillion in September 2023, highlighting the persistent demand for physical cash despite the expansion of electronic payment channels in the country. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics, also showed that currency outside banks increased by 10.3 per cent year-on-year from N4.465 trillion in September 2025 to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. The figures indicate that cash held outside the banking system has more than doubled in three years, reflecting the scale of currency demand within the economy and the challenges facing efforts to deepen the use of formal banking and electronic payment systems. A breakdown of the data showed that currency outside banks increased by 66.2 per cent from N2.416 trillion in September 2023 to N4.016 trillion in September 2024. The figure subsequently rose to N4.465 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 11.2 per cent from the corresponding period in 2024, before climbing further to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. According to analysts, the latest increase indicates that the preference for cash transactions remains significant, notwithstanding the growing adoption of mobile banking, electronic transfers, point-of-sale terminals and other digital payment platforms. Demand deposits rise 71% Meanwhile, demand deposits in the banking system increased by 70.8 per cent to N39.124 trillion in September 2026 from N22.903 trillion in September 2023. The CBN data showed that demand deposits rose to N31.842 trillion in September 2024, representing an increase of 39.0 per cent against the corresponding period in 2023. The figure climbed further to N34.642 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 8.8 per cent year-on-year, before rising to N39.124 trillion in September 2026, representing a 12.9 per cent increase over September 2025. The growth in demand deposits indicates an expansion in funds held in bank accounts that are generally accessible for payments and withdrawals on demand. Reacting to this data, Clifford Egbomeade, Economic and Communications expert, said: “The simultaneous increase in demand deposits and currency outside banks points to the coexistence of formal banking balances and substantial demand for physical cash in Nigeria’s payment system. ‘‘However, the two indicators measure different components of monetary activity. Demand deposits represent bank-account balances, while currency outside banks represents cash held outside the banking system. ‘‘Their growth rates alone do not establish how much of the increase in cash holdings is attributable to economic growth, inflation, informal transactions or changes in payment preferences.” Vanguard News The post Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN appeared first on Vanguard New

item.title: Women in Politics: Nigeria’s political structure not built for women — Adeola Azeez
item.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou As Nigeria prepares for another general election in 2027, the question of women’s participation in politics and access to elective offices remains a subject for debate. Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters Adeola Azeez, a daughter of the late Afenifere leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo and one of the Founders of Women in Management, Business & Public Service, WIMBIZ, a founding member of Women in Politics (WIMPol) and a former Deputy Country Representative, Nigeria, of Deutsch e-Bank; was recently declared winner at the Ijebu Central Federal Consistency primary election on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Ogun State. In this interview, she speaks on her experience contesting for the House of Representatives, the challenges of securing a party ticket, the influence of party structures on women’s political ambitions and her determination to contest again in 2027. She also discusses the need for women who have secured elective positions to support aspiring female politicians and explains why she believes women must remain committed to political participation despite the barriers they face. Excerpts: You transitioned from the corporate world to politics after your retirement in 2020. What informed that decision? I have always believed in the importance of women’s participation in leadership. By the time I retired in 2020, I had prepared myself for a career in politics. From 2013, I knew that politics was something I wanted to pursue, so I began preparing for it. I eventually contested for the House of Representatives in 2023 to represent Ogbomoso Central Federal Constituency. I approached the contest with the same seriousness, preparation and determination as any other candidate. What were the major challenges you encountered as a woman contesting for political office? The challenges women face in politics are well known. They include political violence, limited access to funding and other barriers. Interestingly, funding was not a major challenge for me because of my corporate experience and the relationships I had built over the years. Having supported, mentored and nurtured women in business, I had established a strong network of sponsors and supporters. My reputation also helped me attract people who believed in my ambition. However, the major challenge was the political structure itself. Nigeria’s political system is not structured to accommodate women adequately. Despite your corporate experience, network and supporters, you did not secure your party’s ticket in 2023. What went wrong? I believe the challenge was the party structure and the people who control access to political opportunities. item.title: 2027: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse — Mutfwang
item.description: •Declares no vacancy in Aso Rock, Plateau Govt House •Says no rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Plateau State governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu inherited an economy that was tottering on the brink of collapse from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023. Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters He also declared there was no vacancy in the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock) and Plateau Government House in 2027, equally dismissing any talks of rainbow coalition. Mutfwang, who stated this during the formal inauguration of All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council in Jos yesterday, also defended Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home. And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money. “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades. Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said. He alleged further that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming more than N30 trillion was printed. Governor Mutfwang said: “When the President took over in 2023, the government he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank. “They printed over N30 trillion which went down the drain. Today, by the grace of God, Central Bank has stabilised and that deficit has been done away with.’’ On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents. “I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. item.title: Give Tinubu, Otu another term for Bakassi seaport, coastal highway — Shettima
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu CALABAR — Vice President Kashim Shettima has assured Cross River residents that the proposed Bakassi Deep Seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway will be delivered, urging them to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027. Shettima gave the assurance yesterday while representing Tinubu at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Calabar. He thanked the people of Cross River for supporting the administration over the past three years, describing the relationship between the government and the electorate as “an alliance of prosperity, an alliance of opportunity.” “Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said. The Vice President urged voters to renew the mandates of Tinubu, Otu and APC candidates seeking election into the National Assembly and the state House of Assembly. He said the party was seeking another mandate based on its stewardship, stressing that elected officials must account to the people who entrusted them with power. On infrastructure, Shettima said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway would link coastal communities, ease the movement of goods and people, boost tourism and attract investment to the region. He added that the project would create thousands of direct and indirect jobs, while opening up economic opportunities for communities along the corridor. On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, the Vice President said the project had received Federal Government approval, expressing optimism that it would become an international maritime gateway upon completion. “When completed, it will become an international maritime gateway. It will attract shipping companies. It will generate employment,” he said. Shettima said the seaport and coastal highway were central to efforts to position Cross River as a major beneficiary of Nigeria’s maritime economy. On education, he said the government’s student financing initiative would promote human capital development, reduce the financial burden on parents and expand access to higher education. item.title: FG disburses N75bn to 104 manufacturers, N65.8bn to MSMEs
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Federal Government has fully disbursed the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion has been disbursed to 15,018 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to boost domestic production, expand businesses and create jobs. Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole, disclosed this in an address on “Harnessing Nigeria’s Economic Potential for Greater Prosperity”. Oduwole said the interventions were part of the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen local industries, improve productive capacity and drive sustainable economic growth. The disbursements were made under the Federal Government’s N200 billion intervention package, managed by the Bank of Industry (BoI), to support businesses, boost domestic production and create jobs. The package comprises the N50 billion Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme for nano businesses, the N75 billion FGN MSME Intervention Fund for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and the N75 billion FGN Manufacturing Sector Fund for manufacturing businesses. Oduwole noted that the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund had been fully disbursed to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion had been disbursed to 15,018 businesses under the MSME Intervention Fund as of the first quarter of 2026. She, however, stressed that the impact of government funding should be measured by stronger businesses, increased production and improved livelihoods rather than the amount disbursed alone. The minister acknowledged that access to finance remained a major challenge for manufacturers seeking to acquire equipment, purchase raw materials, expand production capacity and create employment. She said Nigeria’s economic transformation required fiscal discipline, monetary stability and policies that supported domestic production and competitiveness. According to her, the government is working to remove barriers to investment, production and trade while creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive. Highlighting developments in the manufacturing sector, Oduwole said cement manufacturing grew by 11.53 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, while motor vehicle assembly expanded by 5.44 per cent during the period. She added that vehicle assembly grew by 40.6 per cent in 2025, while cassava starch production recorded growth of 474.74 per cent. “Processing locally grown cassava into industrial starch will support manufacturers, while vehicle assembly will create opportunities for engineers, technicians and supply-chain businesses,” she said. The minister also highlighted opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), noting that intra-African trade had grown by 21 per cent. item.title: YPP’s Agada wants end to raw material exports
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arch. Peter Agada, has called for an end to the export of Nigeria’s raw materials without adding value, saying the practice deprives the country of greater economic benefits. Agada spoke in an interview in Abuja on Monday while outlining his economic blueprint ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said his proposed administration would prioritise electricity supply and promote industrialisation from the ward level to ensure that value was added to Nigerian produce before export. “The industrialisation we all talk about can only happen when we fix power and put in place policies that will promote investments from the ward level upwards,” Agada said. He said rural communities would be made attractive to agro-allied industries capable of processing agricultural produce for export and generating foreign exchange. “Our rural communities will attract agro-allied industries to promote export of produce after value has been added to earn foreign exchange. Enough of sending raw materials only to collect peanuts in return,” he said. The YPP candidate also said his proposed administration would mobilise Nigerians at home and in the diaspora to build a country citizens would be proud to call home. He said this would involve building on the country’s strengths while addressing areas of weakness. On politics, Agada urged members of the political elite, irrespective of party affiliation, to allow Nigerians to freely choose their leaders at all levels. He said the practice of imposing leaders on the electorate on the basis of ethnic or religious considerations should become a thing of the past. item.title: Customs appoints Mamman Ali acting Adamawa/Taraba Comptroller
item.description: By Umar Yusuf, Yola The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has appointed Deputy Comptroller Mamman Ali as the Acting Area Comptroller of its Adamawa/Taraba Command. Ali, who was until his appointment the Coordinator of the Customs Anti-Smuggling Unit, Operation Whirlwind, Zone E, takes over from Mohammed Tako, who has been promoted to Assistant Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of Zone B, Kaduna. At a brief handing-over ceremony in Yola on Monday, Tako said the command recorded significant achievements during his tenure despite directives on strict border closure. He said the command strengthened security along critical border corridors through enhanced joint operations and patrols with sister security agencies. Tako disclosed that the total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of seizures recorded by the command during his one-year tenure stood at ₦535,975,190. He commended officers and men of the command for their cooperation during his tenure and urged them to extend the same support to his successor. In his remarks, the new Acting Area Comptroller, Ali, pledged to build on the achievements of his predecessor. He solicited the support and cooperation of sister security agencies, officers and men of the command to strengthen border policing and curb smuggling activities across Adamawa and Taraba states. item.title: Ogun 2027: Adebutu dismisses INEC list omission
item.description: ….Receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has described the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that it would not stop him from contesting the 2027 election. Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s state secretariat in Abeokuta. The defectors were led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, and received by Adebutu alongside other party leaders, including the PDP’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo. Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP. He cited his participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades as evidence of his loyalty and challenged those questioning his membership to provide evidence that he had defected. “I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked. Adebutu also said he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun, which he claimed recorded more than 19,800 members. He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing it as further evidence of his continued membership of the party. The PDP chieftain alleged that the controversy over his omission from the INEC list was intended to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters. He, however, urged party members to remain focused, saying the development would not disrupt the PDP’s mobilisation activities across the state. Adebutu disclosed that the party’s campaign team had visited 12 of the state’s 20 local government areas and more than 140 of its 236 wards. He said the grassroots mobilisation exercise would continue despite what he described as attempts to distract the party. “We have visited 12 of the 20 local governments. Of the 236 wards, we have visited over 140. Tomorrow, we continue again because we know that the trick is to get us distracted. We will not be distracted. We will keep our eyes on the ball, and we shall win,” he said. Earlier, William said the defectors decided to leave the APC because of their dissatisfaction with the party’s approach to governance and what he described as its failure to uphold democratic principles and deliver development in Ogun State. item.title: Inca children were drugged before being sacrificed
item.description: Figurines found alongside child mummies at Llullaillaco, on the Argentina-Chile border, and Ampato, Peru J. Reinhard Young children selected to be sacrificed as part of elaborate Inca rituals were given psychedelic and intoxicating substances, possibly to relieve the terror of their imminent death or in the belief that the drugs would help them communicate with the gods. “We cannot reconstruct the children’s emotions or determine precisely how they experienced these events,” says Dagmara Socha at the University of Warsaw, Poland. “However, we should not assume that being selected for a prestigious religious ceremony necessarily meant that the experience was not frightening or traumatic.” Read more Surprising skeletons prompt a radical rethink of Egyptian pyramids The Inca kingdom dominated 4000 kilometres of the west coast of South America from the late 13th century until the Spanish conquest of the 16th century. Advertisement In a ritual known as capacocha, children and young women were sacrificed to the mountain gods. According to an account by Spanish friar Martín de Murúa, written in 1590 , the capacocha ceremony was conducted to ensure there would be “no famine nor lack of fruits of the earth, nor would there be drought, nor pestilence, nor rebellion”. Socha and her colleagues studied eight frozen, mummified children, seven of whom were girls, discovered between the 1920s and 90s at sites in Peru, Argentina and Chile. They are thought to have been aged between 6 and 14 when they died. It is thought some were killed with sharp weapons, while others were buried alive, says Socha. Archaeologists beginning to excavate one of the mummies on the summit of Llullaillaco mountain J. Reinhard The researchers analysed the mummies’ hair and nail samples to determine which psychoactive plants were given to children during the capacocha ritual. Toxicological screening detected cocaine in all the hair samples, along with markers of alcohol and coca leaf chewing in half of the individuals. The team also identified harmine, a hallucinogenic compound found in the ceremonial drink ayahuasca, in one of the nail samples. Subscriber-only newsletter Sign up to Our Human Story Sign up to newsletter Socha and her colleagues suggest that the antidepressant properties of harmine could have been used to calm the children and maintain a positive mood. Each sacrifice seemed to be associated with a unique chemical signature preserved in the child’s hair and nails. This may indicate that each child was “prepared” in a different way, perhaps to direct their sacrifice towards a specific deity. “We are beginning to understand capacocha not simply as a single sacrificial event, but as a complex process involving extensive preparations, long journeys and different ritual practices,” says Socha. Journal Reference: Antiquity DOI: 10.15184/aqy.2026.10439

item.title: Diri urges Bayelsa governorship aspirants to seek God
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa YENAGOA — Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has urged anyone aspiring to succeed him to seek God’s approval through prayer, saying the next governor must be a God-fearing person. Diri spoke on Monday during the state’s 15th Thanksgiving service at the Ecumenical Centre, Igbogene, Yenagoa, where he declared that Bayelsa had been handed over to God. He said nobody could stop anyone chosen by God to lead the state, adding that the Almighty would always have the final say in its affairs. The governor also urged residents to remain united, tolerant and peaceful, describing these as essential conditions for the state’s development. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the lives of residents, saying it had the political will to transform Bayelsa, which he described as one of the states with the best environments for development. Diri thanked the people for their support over the past six years and urged them to sustain their cooperation with the government. “All who want to be governor, go and seek the face of God. Anyone who wants to be governor must be God-fearing. If God said yes, nobody can say no, not even me,” he said. He added: “Let us continue to worship God. Let us be tolerant and patient as we will become victorious at the end of the day. “As I keep saying, those of us who were born in Yenagoa or know Bayelsa of old can see the difference today. It is enough to give thanks. “We have one of the best environments in Nigeria, and with the political will, we are bringing development to our people.” In his sermon, the guest preacher and former Bayelsa State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, Very Rev. Joseph Opelema, urged Christians to combine their religious faith with responsible citizenship. Speaking on the theme, “Called to be Good Christians and Good Citizens,” Opelema said Christians had dual responsibilities as members of the church and citizens of society. Drawing his message from Matthew 22:15-22, where Jesus addressed the question of paying taxes, he said the biblical instruction to give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God underscored the importance of responsible citizenship. The cleric said Christians should demonstrate sacrifice, prudence, accountability, justice, love, care and charity wherever they found themselves, particularly in public office. He lamented what he described as a gap between religious participation and the practice of Christian values, urging believers to become witnesses, the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Opelema also described Bayelsa as richly endowed with natural and human resources, favourable weather, land and rivers, which he said could make the state a tourism destination. He expressed optimism that the state could realise its potential with God-fearing leadership. item.title: Anthropic's compute tab could top $1T as Q3 revenue nears $17B
item.description: Anthropic has published a regulatory filing revealing nearly $900 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments, with additional estimated payments potentially pushing the total beyond $1 trillion. The Monday filing reports that Anthropic expects to pay nearly $70 billion in contractual obligations by September 2027, with a total of roughly $447.5 billion in commitments expected to be incurred by the end of 2030. That's assuming of course its revenues continue their upward trajectory, which the prospectus warns is far from guaranteed. "In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our revenue was $33.2 billion, representing a year-over-year growth rate of 1,206%," the prospectus reads. "We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all." "Our ability to meet the substantial and growing financial obligations of these requirements to secure compute depends on our ability to generate significant revenue growth," the filing reads. Which is to say, if Anthropic's revenues don't grow faster than its compute commitments, it could end up falling into a nasty spiral. And while Anthropic has several options, including debt and equity financing, relying on these long term could dilute existing shareholders or force the company to borrow on unfavorable terms. Every IPO filing reads a bit like this because no company can guarantee eternal success and growth. A lot of this filing's language, as damning as it might sound, is therefore just Anthropic covering its butt. However, even though the company is still growing steadily year-over-year, the latest filing shows revenue growth is already slowing. Between Q1 and Q2 of this year, revenues grew nearly 2.5x. Yet in Q3, Anthropic's reported revenues of nearly $17 billion represented an increase of just 46 percent from Q2. In the same period, Anthropic's compute and infrastructure costs grew 77 percent and it kept signing deals that commit it to more expenditure. Last week, we reported that Anthropic's purchase commitments exceeded $800 billion over the next decade or so. Anthropic now says its commitments are closer to $895 billion. Roughly $320 billion of those commitments relate to existing contractual obligations. Another $451 billion covers leases Anthropic has signed, but that have yet to commence, with the company expecting them to begin between 2026 and 2028, although some remain subject to termination rights or other conditions. Overall, however, Anthropic's compute spend is on track to increase substantially over the next few years. And that's not even counting the blank checks Anthropic has written to secure adequate compute, which it values at $150-$175 billion, putting Anthropic's total compute tab at somewhere north of $1 trillion. Anthropic can't walk away from some of this spending because its deals with Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Broadcom, which now total $437 billion, are non-cancellable. Some require payme

item.title: North Korea slams FBI allegations over Binance hack as ‘grave’ provocation
item.description: North Korea on Tuesday slammed the FBI’s allegations that Pyongyang was behind the theft of $6 billion from cryptocurrency platform Binance, with Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister labelling it a “grave political provocation”. Kim Yo Jong, in a statement released Tuesday by the KCNA state news agency, said the FBI’s claim was “absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” given prior US allegations that North Korea was behind last year’s major hack of Bybit. “It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds,” Kim said, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name. The FBI said on Saturday that a North Korea-affiliated hacking group called TraderTraitor had been behind the hack. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year, which had been the largest crypto theft until the Binance hack. “This is a sinister attempt to damage the international image of the DPRK and undermine its dignity and national prestige and another grave violation of the sovereignty of the DPRK,” Kim said. “It is the consistent policy stand of the DPRK government to resolutely oppose all sorts of malicious acts in cyberspace,” she added. Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. After the FBI released its statement on Saturday, US President Donald Trump cast doubt on North Korea’s involvement in the hack. “I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida. Trump has made repeated overtures to nuclear-armed North Korea since returning to office, and said he was open to meeting with supreme leader Kim Jong Un this year. Those gestures have been met with silence from Pyongyang. Kim Yo Jong, in her statement, said the new allegations “confirmed Washington’s hostile attitude toward the DPRK once again.” “We have issues to reconsider in diverse aspects as regards the very unpleasant US hostile attitude,” she added. item.title: Max-severity bug in widely used OT programming tool exploited to deliver Linux malware
item.description: Unknown criminals are exploiting a maximum-severity vulnerability in Node-RED, a flow-based programming tool that is widely used in critical infrastructure, to deploy a flow that downloads and runs a Linux bot. Node-RED is commonly used for workflow automation in industrial control systems (ICS) and operational technology (OT) environments. It’s built on top of Node.js and is used in commercial products including Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 . In August, Siemens assigned the vulnerability identifier – CVE-2026-58115 – to describe the bug and explain its perfect 10-out-of-10 CVSS rating. Affected Siemens devices do not enforce authentication on the Node-RED HTTP interface, allowing unauthenticated access to programming nodes that can execute system commands on the device. This means unauthenticated remote attackers can create malicious flows, which is what VulnCheck researchers began documenting last Friday. “On October 30, 2026, one of our canaries caught an attacker exploiting CVE-2026-58115,” VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity warned in a Monday advisory, adding that two Node-RED built-in nodes make this vulnerability “trivial to weaponize.” One is an inject node, which fires a message either on a schedule or once at startup. The second, an exec node, can run shell commands. “Wire one to the other and the flow executes a command as soon as it is deployed, with no further interaction,” Garrity said. Plus, these exploits come as criminals increasingly look to target internet-exposed OT and ICS devices , allowing their cyberattacks to impact the physical world and produce real-life harm. Case in point: the ongoing refrigeration controller hacks across Europe and the attacks on wa ter systems across at least 12 US states over the summer. The activity observed by VulnCheck came from a single IP address, 4.201.105[.]116, which sits in Microsoft’s AS8075 network and geolocates to Brazil. “It didn't just scan us. It sent the complete exploit, flow and dropper, in a single POST /flows,” Garrity wrote. While there’s a lot that the researchers don’t yet know about the attacks - they didn’t retrieve a binary or staged scripts to analyze - the filename, bot-linux-amd64, indicates that the malware targets Linux running on AMD64 processors. It also suggests the malware operator may have other builds. “We did not fetch the binary, so we can't say what it does once running,” Garrity noted. Between October 30 and November 1, the researchers saw this IP address target the same Node-RED vulnerability 16 times, and log 125 hits against eight different CVEs across their wider canary network. Among the targets of the attack were a seven-year-old Apache Solr flaw tracked as CVE-2019-17558 – affecting Camunda, Gitea, MLflow, Traefik, and Joomla, alongside Node-RED. All this suggests “opportunistic mass scanning rather than a targeted attack,” according to the researcher. item.title: Why large dogs age faster than small ones, and other October research highlights
item.description: It’s a regrettable reality that there is never enough time to cover all the interesting scientific stories we come across. So every month, we highlight a handful of the best stories that nearly slipped through the cracks. October’s list includes an epigenetic mechanism for why large dogs age faster than smaller ones; physicists who trapped a single particle of antimatter for months; and invisible tattoo inks that only show up under UV light. Why large dogs age faster In many mammalian species, larger creatures tend to have longer lifespans. Mice, for instance, live an average of just two years, while some whales can last for as long as 200 years. Dogs, however, buck this pattern; larger dogs tend to age faster and die younger than smaller ones, which makes canines an ideal model for biologists to study to learn more about aging in general. Arizona State University scientists report that these lifespan differences seem to be due to so-called "jumping genes," according to a paper published in the journal Science. The authors used data from 864 dogs collected in the Dog Aging Project to map patterns of DNA methylation (which influences how much certain genes are turned on or off) across the entire genome. It's part of the epigenome, whose markers can change over time in response to stress and other environmental factors. Genetic sequences, by contrast, are largely fixed. So DNA methylation is a good chemical indicator of aging and DNA regulation. Read full article Comments
